raw_case_text:
A 55-year-old female patient of afro-descendant was diagnosed with AIDS in 1999, when she developed chronic diarrhea and weight loss. This patient was a homemaker born in Bahia and residing in Serra-ES (Brazil) with an HIV-positive and nonexclusive sexual partner and three children. She had been in menopause for six years at the time of VZV diagnosis. Antiretroviral treatment was initiated with zidovudine (AZT) + didanosine in 2001 because her CD4+ count fell below 350 cells/mm3. Because of noncompliance, she remained without anti-retroviral medication for 31 months, which, in 2008, allowed her to be susceptible to a very aggressive clinical episode of herpes zoster with severe neuralgia, which led to a seven-day hospitalization. Initially, she presented with maculopapular lesions that progressed into vesicles and then pustules and crusts on the right thoracic region following the nerve path (Figure 1 and Figure 2) that lasted for 12 days. Laboratory tests showed a normal complete blood count (CBC), a viral load (VL) of 27,500 copies/mL and a CD4+ T lymphocyte count of 328 cells/mm3.
The patient was treated with intravenous acyclovir for seven days, with marked improvement of the lesions. She started therapy with AZT + lamivudine + abacavir. At the same time, the cervical oncotic cytology was suggestive of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia I (CIN I) and infection with human papillomavirus (HPV). Colposcopy suggested CIN I, and the cytological samples from the cervix after 3, 6, 12, and 18 months were normal. A hypochromic scar remained in the affected area after the herpes zoster was treated (Figures 3A and B), which caused constraints on the patient's social life and affected her quality of life. Moreover, she suffered from persistent post-herpetic neuritis that lasted for 12 months. The patient remains in a clinical follow-up program in the infectious and parasitic diseases sector at a public hospital in Espirito Santo state. Currently, the patient adheres correctly to the antiretroviral therapy and has had no relapses of herpes zoster, and her quality of life has improved significantly.
Above, we described an aggressive form of infection caused by VZV that served as a warning flag for AIDS in a patient who did not adhere to HAART.
The next section describes the factors involved in noncompliance and provides support for a more effective approach to the clinical follow-up of individuals with HIV.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old female presenting with a painful vesicular rash on the right thoracic wall and severe neuralgia for 12 days.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient experienced intense neuropathic pain over the right thoracic dermatome followed by the eruption of maculopapular lesions that rapidly evolved into painful vesicles, pustules, and crusts over a 12-day duration. The neuralgia became excruciating, impairing daily functioning and necessitating hospitalization.
subjective.past_medical_history: History of chronic retroviral disease diagnosed in 1999 following chronic diarrhea and involuntary weight loss; initiated on zidovudine and didanosine in 2001 when CD4 count dropped below 350 cells/mm3; subsequently non-compliant with therapy and off antiretrovirals for 31 months prior to presentation. Menopause for 6 years. Homemaker residing in Serra-ES, Brazil; non-exclusive sexual partner with retroviral infection; mother of three children.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for severe burning neuropathic pain and dermatomal rash; negative for fever, visual changes, or motor deficits. Home medications: none (noncompliant for 31 months). Allergies: unmentioned.

objective.physical_examination: Dermatologic exam: extensive maculopapular lesions, grouped vesicles, pustules, and crusts distributed in a unilateral dermatomal pattern along the right thoracic wall following the intercostal nerve pathway, accompanied by exquisite local hyperalgesia. General physical exam otherwise unremarkable.
objective.routine_investigations: Complete blood count (CBC): normal. Cervical oncotic cytology and colposcopy: cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade I (CIN I) with cellular changes suggestive of human papillomavirus (HPV) (normal on repeat cytology at 3, 6, 12, and 18 months).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Definitive diagnosis: Severe, aggressive multi-dermatomal herpes zoster (varicella-zoster virus reactivation) with protracted post-herpetic neuralgia and cervical intraepithelial neoplasia I (CIN I) in the setting of non-adherent human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) / AIDS (viral load 27,500 copies/mL, CD4+ T-lymphocyte count 328 cells/mm3). Management & Outcome: Hospitalized and treated with intravenous acyclovir for 7 days, resulting in marked drying and crusted resolution of cutaneous lesions. Re-initiated on combination antiretroviral therapy comprising zidovudine (AZT), lamivudine (3TC), and abacavir (ABC). The patient developed persistent post-herpetic neuralgia requiring pain management for 12 months, and retained permanent hypochromic thoracic scarring. At long-term follow-up in the infectious diseases service, patient demonstrated excellent ART adherence with no recurrence of zoster and substantial improvement in quality of life.
